newsitem.title: USA: Active Voice in deal with Siemens, warns about profits.
newsitem.headline: Active Voice in deal with Siemens, warns about profits.

text.p: Telecommunications software and equipment firm Active Voice Corp. said Thursday it expected its profits for the current quarter to be below analysts' expecations, sparking a steep drop in its stock.

The Seattle-based company also announced that it had reached a messaging products pact with a subsidiary of Germany's Siemens AG that is expected to be worth more than $50 million in revenues for Active Voice over six years.
Active Voice stock was down $1.06 at $12.25 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.

The company said its revenues were expected to be 12 percent to 16 percent higher than the year-ago quarter, while earnings should be "slightly up" from a year ago, when the company reported earnings of $668,874, or 14 cents a share, on sales of $11.0 million.
Analysts, however, had expected the company to earn between 27 cents and 29 cents a share in the quarter, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.
The company is to report fourth-quarter results on May 13.
Active Voice, which makes voice processing and computer telecommunications products, cited timing and delay problems for certain orders from larger customers. It gave no details.

In its deal with Siemens Business Communications, Active Voice said, the companies will work on products to connect electronic mail, voice mail, facsimiles and mixed media files, using a system based on Microsoft Corp.'s Windows NT software.
The plan is to provide a single "in-box" so that an executives can call in and have E-mails read or faxed to them, or can use a computer to access voicemail for example.
